I read the [feature description](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/design/feature_descriptions/J_52_speed_up_creating_new_cards.md), analyzed the [Chrome trace](<C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/Trace-new card.json>), and followed the creation and render paths. **The trace does not show every board column refreshing.** It records one `CardColumn` render after `cardAdded`. Most of the visible cost comes from React work around that update and a second wave after persistence.

| Finding | Evidence | Proposed solution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Adding the card triggers a long render | `cardAdded` occurs about 50 ms after the click; the following React render lasts about **182 ms**. The click task lasts about **351 ms** overall. | Keep the update scoped to the affected column. Inspect the card and sortable components rendered within it for avoidable updates; measure again after each change. |
| Completion causes another broad render wave | About **1.3 s** after the click, a `changed` event is followed by React renders of roughly **152, 44, and 133 ms**. The trace shows `AppMenu`, action controls, and `NewCardDialog` work in this wave. | Remove redundant notifications and state updates. In particular, [closeDialog](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/components/shell/project/use_project_toolbar_menu_actions.ts) calls `setError(null)`, and [setError](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/services/project/project_session_service.ts) dispatches `changed` even when the error is already null. Make that operation a no-op when its state is unchanged. Then check whether form reset and dialog close can complete with fewer renders. |
| A watcher echo may do unnecessary project work | [reloadMarkdownFilesFromWatchEvents](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/services/project/project_loading.ts) calls `importExternalCardFiles` after processing watched files; that function plans imports across the supplied file list. Expected writes already have a separate classification path. The trace shows later repository activity, but does **not** prove this scan caused the long render wave. | Instrument this path first. If it runs for the new card’s own write, skip the external-import scan once all watched changes are confirmed unchanged. Preserve handling for genuine external edits. |
| One insertion still scans collection data | [updateFiles](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/services/project/project_state.ts) filters the loaded files and card arrays; [dispatchCardChanges](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/services/data/data_service.ts) builds maps and compares all active cards. [useCardColumnCards](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/components/card_view/use_card_column_cards.ts) also filters cards and orders the target column. | If projects with many cards remain slow after the render fixes, update membership and order through the known changed card instead of scanning the full collection. This is a scaling improvement, not the clearest cause of this trace’s delay. |

The recording came from a Vite development page with extensive React and DevTools instrumentation, so these durations should **not** be treated as production timings. The strongest immediate targets are the repeated menu/dialog renders after completion and the expensive render following `cardAdded`. I made no code changes or ran tests.
